Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Medical Record Number: [REDACTED]
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital Course: 
The patient, a 29-year-old woman with a history of earlobe piercing at a beauty salon six days prior, presented to the hospital with symptoms of headache, fever, and blurred vision. Upon admission, she exhibited multiple skin manifestations, including maculopapular rashes on her face, scattered pustules and microabscesses on her trunk and extremities, and subungual splinter hemorrhages on her fingers. Diagnostic tests revealed microscopic hematuria and low platelet count, in addition to CSF analysis indicating a raised white blood cell count. Multiple embolic infarcts and leptomeningeal enhancement were found through brain magnetic resonance imaging. A transthoracic echocardiography performed on day two revealed vegetations on the anterior chordae of her mitral valve. S aureus, resistant to penicillin and oxacillin, was isolated in her blood cultures. The initial treatment of nafcillin and ceftriaxone was replaced with vancomycin in combination with gentamicin. 

On day six of hospitalization, the patient became hypotensive and dyspneic, leading to the discovery of mitral valve chordae rupture through echocardiography. She underwent an emergency cardiac surgery in which her entire mitral valve was removed and replaced with a prosthetic valve. Gentamicin treatment was discontinued on day eight. Her condition stabilized, and her facial rashes disappeared completely. Follow-up brain and abdominal CT scans indicated an improvement in her condition. After eight weeks of vancomycin therapy, the patient was discharged.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Medications: 
The patient was discharged on vancomycin.

Follow-Up: 
The patient is advised to follow up with the healthcare provider for further treatment and monitoring.

text:
# Principal Diagnosis: **I33.0 – Acute and subacute infective endocarditis**

## Why this is the principal diagnosis

The condition that, after study, chiefly occasioned the admission is **acute bacterial endocarditis of the mitral valve**. It was caused by *Staphylococcus aureus* resistant to oxacillin and penicillin (MRSA), likely seeded from the recent earlobe piercing.

Nearly every other finding in the summary is a manifestation or complication of the endocarditis:
- Septic emboli to the brain, causing embolic infarcts and meningeal involvement
- Skin pustules, microabscesses and splinter haemorrhages
- Haematuria
- Thrombocytopenia
- Chordae rupture

"Sepsis" is not documented as a diagnosis, so A41.0 (sepsis due to *S. aureus*) should not be sequenced first unless the clinician confirms it. If sepsis were documented, ACS sequencing rules for sepsis would need review.

## Suggested additional codes

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| B95.6 | *Staphylococcus aureus* as the cause of disease classified elsewhere |
| U82.1 | Resistance to methicillin (MRSA) |
| I51.1 | Rupture of chordae tendineae, NEC (complication on day 6) |
| I63.4 | Cerebral infarction due to embolism of cerebral arteries |
| G03.9 / G00.3 | Meningitis (CSF pleocytosis with leptomeningeal enhancement; G00.3 if confirmed staphylococcal) |
| D69.6 | Thrombocytopenia, unspecified |
| R31 | Haematuria (if not attributed to a specific coded renal condition) |
| L08.9 / L02.x | Skin pustules or abscesses (septic emboli), if documented as significant |
| R57.x / I95.9 | Hypotension or shock, if documented and meeting ACS 0002 |
| T14.1 / W45 / Y93 | Possibly, to capture the piercing as the source; coder judgement and local policy apply |

**Procedure:** Mitral valve replacement with a prosthetic valve (ACHI block 0628, e.g. 38488-xx), plus cardiopulmonary bypass.

Please verify these codes against the ICD-10-AM/ACHI/ACS edition in use at your facility. Confirm any undocumented diagnoses, such as sepsis or meningitis aetiology, with the treating clinician before assigning them.
